title: Fresh start

clues.t: The Romans once started me in March, which is why September means ‘seventh month’.
Julius Caesar fixed me up, then Pope Gregory fixed me again in 1582.
Britain skipped 11 days of me in 1752.
Every four years I grow by a day.
People hang me on fridges and cross off my squares.
Today you start a brand new one of me.

pearl: The Gregorian calendar dropped 10 days in 1582. Britain and its colonies held out until 1752 and had to skip 11.

title: Pedal power

clues.t: My early ancestor in 1817 had no pedals; riders pushed with their feet.
One famous version had a giant front wheel and a tiny back one.
A chain to the back wheel made me safe.
I’m the most energy-efficient way for a person to travel.
I have two wheels, handlebars and a bell.
You ride me to work or around the park, wearing a helmet.

pearl: The ‘penny-farthing’ was named after a large and a small British coin.

title: Gods’ drink

clues.t: The Maya and Aztecs drank me bitter, sometimes with chilli.
My beans were once used as money.
My scientific name means ‘food of the gods’.
I’m poisonous to dogs.
I melt at about body temperature, which is why I melt in your mouth.
Easter eggs and Tim Tams are made of me.

pearl: Theobroma, cocoa’s genus, means ‘food of the gods’. Theobromine is the part dogs can’t handle.

title: Roof of the world

clues.t: In Nepal I’m called Sagarmatha.
In Tibet I’m called Chomolungma.
I grow a few millimetres a year as India pushes into Asia.
Hillary and Tenzing first stood on top of me in 1953.
I’m 8,849 metres tall.
I’m the highest mountain on Earth.

pearl: Edmund Hillary was a beekeeper from New Zealand. Tenzing Norgay had tried the climb six times before.

title: Busy worker

clues.t: I dance to tell my sisters where the flowers are.
My queen can lay about 2,000 eggs a day.
I beat my wings about 200 times a second, which makes my buzz.
I die after stinging a mammal because my barbed stinger stays behind.
I make wax and store food in six-sided cells.
I make honey.

pearl: A worker bee makes about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in her whole life.

title: Keeper of the light

clues.t: One of me in Alexandria was a wonder of the ancient world.
My keepers often lived alone with their families for years.
Augustin Fresnel’s special lens let my beam reach much further.
Each of me flashes in my own pattern so sailors know which I am.
I’m usually a tall tower on a headland or rock.
I warn ships away from danger at night.

pearl: Fresnel lenses use rings of glass prisms instead of one huge, heavy lens.

title: Cheesy

clues.t: A queen of Italy gave her name to one of my most famous types in 1889.
My most classic version shows the colours of the Italian flag.
Naples says it’s my home.
Hawaiian, with pineapple, was invented in Canada.
I’m round, flat and baked in a very hot oven.
Dough, tomato and mozzarella: I’m often delivered in a box.

pearl: The Margherita was reportedly named after Queen Margherita of Savoy.

title: Night light

clues.t: I always show the same face to Earth.
I’m slowly drifting away by about 4 cm a year.
I pull on the oceans to make tides.
Twelve people have walked on me.
I go from new to full and back every 29 and a half days.
I light up the night sky.

pearl: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed first, in July 1969. The last visit was in 1972.

title: Ring ring

clues.t: Alexander Graham Bell patented me in 1876, just hours before a rival.
My first words were reportedly ‘Mr Watson, come here, I want to see you’.
Operators once connected every call by hand.
My Australian emergency number is 000.
Some of me had rotary dials; now most are smartphones.
You use me to call people.

pearl: Elisha Gray lodged a similar idea at the US patent office on the same day as Bell.

title: Checkmate

clues.t: I began in India about 1,500 years ago.
My queen used to be one of my weakest pieces.
A computer called Deep Blue beat the world champion at me in 1997.
The number of possible games of me is bigger than the atoms in the universe.
I have 64 squares and 32 pieces.
Kings, queens, rooks, bishops, knights and pawns.

pearl: The queen became the most powerful piece in Spain around the 1490s.

title: Rainy day

clues.t: Ancient Egyptians and Chinese used me against the sun first.
In 18th-century London, men carrying me were mocked.
A man named Jonas Hanway made me fashionable for men.
My ribs and canopy fold away.
The wind loves turning me inside out.
You open me when it rains.

pearl: ‘Umbrella’ comes from the Latin umbra, meaning shadow.

title: Brew

clues.t: Legend says I fell into an emperor’s boiling water in China.
A tax on me helped spark the American Revolution.
Green, black and oolong all come from the same plant.
Britain once traded opium to buy me.
I’m made from the leaves of Camellia sinensis.
Milk or no milk? A cuppa.

pearl: The Boston Tea Party of 1773 dumped 342 chests of it into the harbour.

title: Hot stuff

clues.t: I buried Pompeii in AD 79.
Iceland has lots of me.
The biggest one of me in the solar system is on Mars.
I can make new islands, like Hawaii.
Molten rock called lava flows out of me.
I’m a mountain that erupts.

pearl: Olympus Mons on Mars is about two and a half times the height of Mount Everest.

title: Unicorn of the sea

clues.t: Medieval Europeans sold my tooth as unicorn horn.
My ‘horn’ is actually a tooth that can grow 3 metres long.
My tooth has millions of nerve endings.
I live in the Arctic and dive under the ice.
I’m a small whale with a spiral tusk.
I’m called the unicorn of the sea.

pearl: Queen Elizabeth I reportedly had a ‘unicorn horn’ cup that was really a narwhal tusk.

title: Click

clues.t: My name comes from Danish words meaning ‘play well’.
A carpenter in Denmark started my company in 1932.
My clutch power is so good that bricks from 1958 still fit today’s ones.
Stepping on me barefoot is famously painful.
I come in sets and little yellow minifigures.
Plastic bricks that click together.

pearl: ‘Leg godt’ means ‘play well’. Lego also means ‘I assemble’ in Latin, though that was a coincidence.

title: Jumping flea

clues.t: Portuguese migrants brought my ancestor to Hawaii in 1879.
My name is often translated as ‘jumping flea’.
I have four strings.
I’m smaller than a guitar.
I’m strongly linked with Hawaiian music.
A small four-stringed instrument you strum.

pearl: The name may describe how fast players’ fingers jumped across the strings.

title: Lucky mould

clues.t: I was found by accident on a dirty dish left over a holiday.
Alexander Fleming noticed me in 1928.
An Australian, Howard Florey, helped turn me into a medicine.
I was mass-produced in time for D-Day in 1944.
I came from a mould called Penicillium.
I was the first antibiotic.

pearl: Florey, from Adelaide, shared the 1945 Nobel Prize with Fleming and Ernst Chain.

title: Little devil

clues.t: My screams scared early European settlers.
I have one of the strongest bites for my size of any mammal.
A contagious facial cancer has made me endangered.
I eat bones, fur and all.
I live only in Tasmania today.
I’m a black marsupial with a big temper and a cartoon namesake.

pearl: Devil facial tumour disease spreads through bites: the cancer cells themselves are passed on.

title: Raw deal

clues.t: I began as a way of preserving fish in fermented rice.
In my modern form I was fast food in Edo, now Tokyo.
The rice in me is seasoned with vinegar.
California rolls are an American invention of mine.
Seaweed, rice and often raw fish.
Japanese food you might dip in soy sauce.

pearl: Early forms fermented the fish in rice for months and threw the rice away.

title: Floating city

clues.t: I’m built on more than 100 small islands.
My buildings stand on millions of wooden piles driven into mud.
Marco Polo was born in me.
I have about 400 bridges and no cars.
Gondolas carry visitors along my canals.
Italian city of canals.

pearl: Underwater wooden piles don’t rot because there’s too little oxygen in the mud.

title: Lost city

clues.t: I was built around 1450 for an Inca emperor.
The Spanish conquerors never found me.
An American explorer made me famous in 1911.
My stones fit so tightly without mortar that a knife won’t slide between them.
I sit high in the Andes above a river valley.
Inca ruins in Peru.

pearl: Hiram Bingham brought world attention to the site, though local farmers knew it well.

title: Twist and turn

clues.t: A Hungarian architecture professor made me in 1974 to teach 3D thinking.
It took my inventor a month to solve me the first time.
I have about 43 quintillion possible positions.
Any position of me can be solved in 20 moves or fewer.
Six faces, nine squares each, six colours.
A twisty puzzle cube.

pearl: Ernő Rubik called it the ‘Magic Cube’ at first.

title: Up, up and away

clues.t: A sheep, a duck and a rooster were my first passengers in 1783.
Two French brothers, the Montgolfiers, launched me.
I have no steering: I go where the wind takes me.
Pilots change height to find winds going the right way.
A burner heats the air inside my envelope.
A giant colourful balloon with a basket.

pearl: The first animal flight lasted about 8 minutes, watched by King Louis XVI.

title: Licked and stuck

clues.t: My first version, the Penny Black, appeared in 1840.
Britain doesn’t print its name on me, only the monarch’s head.
Collectors call themselves philatelists.
A rare one of me sold for millions of dollars.
You stick me in the corner of an envelope.
A small sticker that pays for posting a letter.

pearl: Britain was first, so it’s still the only country allowed to leave its name off.

title: No brain needed

clues.t: I have no brain, heart or bones.
I’ve been around for more than 500 million years.
One of me can, in a sense, age backwards.
Vinegar is used for some of my stings, but not all.
Australia has some of my deadliest kinds, like the box.
A see-through sea creature that stings.

pearl: Turritopsis dohrnii can revert to its young polyp stage, earning it the name ‘immortal jellyfish’.

title: Smashed

clues.t: My name comes from an Aztec word.
I’m technically a large berry with one seed.
I ripen only after being picked.
I was once called an alligator pear.
My flesh is green and creamy; my skin can be bumpy.
Smashed on toast at brunch.

pearl: Avocados are toxic to some pets and birds because of a substance called persin.

title: Squeeze box

clues.t: Versions of me were played across Europe and the Middle East for centuries.
My bag was once made from a sheep or goat skin.
I have drones that play one note the whole time.
I’m often played at funerals and Burns Night.
You blow air into my bag and squeeze it out through pipes.
A Scottish instrument with a loud, wailing sound.

pearl: The Great Highland bagpipe has three drones and a chanter that plays the tune.

title: Coconut cube

clues.t: I’m said to be named after a governor of Queensland.
One story says I was made by accident when sponge was dropped in chocolate.
New Zealand also claims to have invented me.
Some of me have jam or cream in the middle.
I’m a sponge square dipped in chocolate.
Rolled in desiccated coconut.

pearl: Lord Lamington was Governor of Queensland from 1896 to 1901, and reportedly disliked the cakes.

title: Lunch

clues.t: An English earl supposedly asked for me so he could keep playing cards.
My earl’s family name is a town in Kent.
Some of me are toasted; some are cut into triangles.
The Reuben, the club and the BLT are famous versions of me.
Two slices of bread with a filling.
You might pack me for lunch.

pearl: John Montagu, the 4th Earl of Sandwich, gave his title to the snack.

title: Famous smile

clues.t: I was stolen in 1911 and missing for two years.
I have no eyebrows.
I’m painted on a poplar wood panel.
I live behind bulletproof glass in the Louvre.
Leonardo da Vinci painted me.
A portrait with a mysterious smile.

pearl: An Italian handyman stole it, believing it should be returned to Italy.

title: After the rain

clues.t: Isaac Newton named my seven colours.
You can only see me with the sun behind you.
Every person sees a slightly different one of me.
Sometimes there are two of me, with the colours flipped in the second.
Sunlight splits into colours in raindrops.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

pearl: From an aeroplane you can sometimes see a rainbow as a full circle.
